name: Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali
nameAr: جرير بن عبد الله بن جابر البجلي القسري رضي الله عنه

laqab.en: 'the Yusuf of this community', Umar's phrase for his beauty

nisbas.en: al-Qasri (of Qasr, a clan of Bajilah)

diedNote: 51 AH (Khalifa and others; the Taqrib adds 'and it is said later'); Ibn al-Kalbi: 54.

deathVariants.authority: Khalifa ibn Khayyat and others; Ibn Hajar, Taqrib
deathVariants.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, letter jim, entry 115; Taqrib al-Tahdhib 915

deathVariants.authority: variant listed in the Shamela narrator record

residence: Qarqisiya (on the Euphrates), after withdrawing from the conflict between Ali and Mu'awiyah

taqrib.ar: صحابي مشهور، مات سنة إحدى وخمسين وقيل بعدها
taqrib.en: A well-known Companion; died in 51, or, it is said, later.

teachers.name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
teachers.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib: 'he narrated from the Prophet ﷺ and from Umar and Mu'awiyah'

students.name: his son Ibrahim ibn Jarir
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (al-Dhahabi: 'he did not meet him')

students.name: his grandson Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir
students.nameAr: أبو زرعة بن عمرو بن جرير
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib; Sunan Abi Dawud 4945; Sunan al-Nasa'i 4157

verdicts.ar: يرحمك الله، نعم السيد كنت في الجاهلية، ونعم السيد أنت في الإسلام
verdicts.en: God have mercy on you: what a fine chief you were in the time of ignorance, and what a fine chief you are in Islam.

verdicts.via: Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Jarir
verdicts.en: Jarir is the Yusuf of this community.
verdicts.source: al-Dhahabi, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala'; the phrase is bracketed into the Taqrib entry in the Wikisource transcription

verdicts.ar: رأيت جرير بن عبد الله وكان وجهه شقة قمر
verdicts.en: I saw Jarir ibn Abdullah, and his face was like a slice of the moon.

companionCounts.source: al-Dhahabi, Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' ('his musnad is about a hundred hadith with repetition; the two shaykhs agree on eight, al-Bukhari alone has two and Muslim alone six'); Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, fasl 10 ('Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali: ten hadith'). The class notes, citing al-Khazraji's Khulasa, give one for al-Bukhari alone; not checked against the Khulasa.

flags.label: When he embraced Islam
flags.detail: Ibn Sa'd: in the year the Prophet ﷺ died; al-Baghawi and Ibn Hibban: Ramadan of the year 10. Ibn Hajar rejects Ibn Abd al-Barr's 'forty days before the Prophet's death', since the Prophet told him at the Farewell Pilgrimage to bid the people be silent, and the Sahihayn report from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he became Muslim after Surat al-Ma'idah came down. Ibn Hajar also rejects al-Tabarani's report that he came to the Prophet at the very start of the mission, as its narrator Husayn ibn Umar al-Ahmasi is weak.

bio: Chief of Bajilah in Yemen before and after his Islam, which he embraced in Ramadan of the year 10, arriving in Madinah with a hundred and fifty of his people. The Prophet ﷺ never saw him without smiling and sent him to demolish Dhu al-Khalasa, the 'Yemeni Ka'ba' of Khath'am. He settled in Kufa, commanded Bajilah in the Iraq campaigns under Umar, and was Ali's envoy to Mu'awiyah; he then withdrew from both sides to Qarqisiya, saying he would not live in a town where Uthman was reviled. He pledged to the Prophet ﷺ on sincere counsel to every Muslim, and kept it in his dealings. He died in 51, or 54.
